title: Sicilian Defense: Closed Variation
line: White keeps the center closed and builds up on the king's side; Black's pieces take the long diagonal and the center.

steps.text: Here White brings the knight out first and does not open the center.
Bring the knight out. It watches d4.

also.e7e6: That also works. This lesson goes on with the knight.
also.d7d6: That also works. This lesson goes on with the knight.

steps.text: Push the pawn on g7 one square, to make room for your bishop.
Put the bishop on g7. It looks along the long diagonal toward White's queen's side.
Push the pawn on d7 one square. It guards e5 and opens a path for your other bishop.
Push the pawn on e7 one square. It guards d5 and f5 against White's pawns.
Bring the other knight to e7, where it does not block your bishop.
Castle. Your king goes to safety, and a rook comes toward the center.
Jump into d4 with the knight. Your pawn on c5 guards it, and it eyes f3 and c2.
steps.after: The knight sits in the center, guarded by your pawn, and hits the knight on f3.

summary: In the Closed Sicilian both sides put a bishop on the long diagonal, and Black's knight finds a home in the center.
